name: Hand-crank gear train
description: Three spur gears on a base plate: turn the crank and the gears pass the motion along, slowing it down and reversing it at every mesh.
how_it_works: You turn the crank, which spins the small 12-tooth driver gear.
The driver meshes with the 24-tooth middle gear. Twice the teeth means it turns at half the speed, in the opposite direction, with twice the torque.
The middle gear meshes with the 18-tooth output gear, which turns 4/3 as fast as the middle gear and in the same direction as the crank.
Overall ratio: output turns 2/3 of a turn for every crank turn. The pointer on the output gear shows it.
All gears share a 4 mm module, so their teeth are the same size and mesh cleanly; each pair sits exactly one radius plus the other apart.
assumptions: Gears spin freely on fixed steel shafts pressed into the base plate.
